# Decision after review round 3 (record 35): how a tie between equal anchors is broken

Asked in this session on 2 October 2026 and answered by Ruud: tie-break by line, then id.

A later finding is offered first to the earlier findings it shares more texts with
(record 30). Among anchors sharing the same number of texts, the one whose raw
`file` reference, line included, equals the finding's comes first, then the one
with the same id, then journal order. The ordering only chooses among anchors the
content already matched; it never creates a join, so the id still never makes two
findings one, which is what the amendment's sentence on the id protects. The
amendment is given a sentence saying so.

Considered and not taken: accepting the tie as a named residue beside SEEN-006's
R-04 (it loses a severity, which the old key got right), and the line alone
without the id (a finding that moved lines between rounds still ties).
